To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the Cooking Lake moraines contain molluscs that are characteristic of the early postglacial period, and 2) the molluscs were deposited between 10 000 and 9000 years ago, during the time interval when the ice sheet was retreating.

the molluscan fauna of the Cooking Lake region, south-central Alberta, indicates the final stages of ice sheet retreat, and that the mollusc assemblages are similar to those found in the southwestern Alberta region during the same time interval.

the Cooking Lake moraines are the youngest of the major ice-marginal landforms of the continental Wisconsin ice advance in south-central Alberta, and the youngest of the moraine complexes in the region to be studied in detail for the molluscan evidence of late Wisconsin glaciation and deglaciation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of molluscs in the reconstruction of the late glacial and postglacial environments in southwestern Alberta and south-central Alberta, and with the correlation between the molluscan faunas in the two regions.
the reconstruction of the paleoenvironmental conditions during the late Wisconsin glaciation in the southern part of the Canadian Prairies, based on the evidence provided by the fossil record.

the use of mollusc faunas to determine the timing of deglaciation and to provide evidence of the climatic ameliorations that occurred at the end of the Wisconsin glacial episode in the Canadian Rockies and adjacent plains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the late Wisconsin ice sheet in the Canadian Rockies and adjacent areas was probably in a state of retreat by 13 000 years BP, and was completely gone by 9000 years ago.
the Wisconsin ice sheet in Alberta was in retreat by at least 10 000 years ago, and that the final melting of the ice sheet in this area occurred over at least the past 2000 years.
, in Alberta at least, the late glacial period began about 13 000 years BP, and ended about 9000 years ago.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the late glacial and early postglaciation in southwestern Alberta was characterized by relatively warm summers and cold winters.
the late Wisconsin ice sheet in Alberta melted from the southwest to the northeast, with the final melting in the Cooking Lake region occurring 10 000 – 9500 years ago.
a period of climatic warming occurred in southwestern Alberta at about 11 500 years BP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Cooking Lake region was deglaciated and occupied by a large lake by 10 900 years BP.
molluscan communities can be used to reconstruct paleoclimates, and that molluscs can be used to date the final melting of the ice sheets in Alberta, Canada.
, in the absence of radiocarbon dating, the use of fossil mollusc communities can be used as a proxy to identify the timing of the end of the last glacial period in western North America.
